kiki.name: Kiki
kiki.summary: v5 (owner review 11-17): soft, lighter brown eye patches instead of raccoon rings; faint darker back bands; on all fours a lower, longer body with hunched shoulders (Species.hunch). Expressions now change the face: happy has smiling (lower-lid) eyes and a raised mouth, surprised has wide eyes, shrunk pupils and lifted brows.
kiki.motion: she walks on all fours, turns toward the camera, rises back into the sentinel (her sit/stand), turns her head left and right, runs through every expression, then says her line
open: Your call needed: the cloud reviewer (11-18) reads the lower, longer, hunched body on all fours as a weasel/mongoose from the side and prefers v4's shorter, higher-shouldered body. v5 follows your note; say which way.
Appeal 7: the critic still wants more charm in the face before 'ready'.
The patches are deliberately soft; at 96 px they read as shading round the eyes rather than a mask.

Feet: fixed in the rig. Each foot hangs level from the ankle (DECISIONS #69) and the meerkat's hind paws pivot at the heel into the sentinel (#70), so `foot_plant` is now a hard check and passes for all five (planted soles stray 1.6-23 mm per stance, all under half the foot's radius). The motion clip here predates the fix until the laptop re-renders the stress takes.
kiki.runners: Both runner-ups are small head/eye/ear morphs from the re-run loop, scored 10.0 without a species read, so they aren't comparable with the current design's score.
kiki.ask: which body on all fours: v5 (your note: lower, longer, hunched) or v4's shorter, higher-shouldered one (the reviewer reads v5 as a weasel)

zuri.name: Zuri
zuri.summary: v3 (owner review 11-17): a stockier zebra: deeper chest, thicker neck and legs, a bigger head, a short bristly striped mane that follows the neck from withers to poll (a lofted ridge skinned to the neck, so it bends with it), real hooves (flat sole, sloped front wall, narrower coronet). Lids drawn up at rest; expressions change the face as for all five.
open: Hard failure, recorded honestly: on the silhouette alone I read 'zebra, but a donkey is the nearest other read', and the rubric counts that as ambiguous with a known confusion (donkey). The thumbnail reads as a zebra. The pony read from v2 is gone.
Appeal 7: the face is calm but not yet charming at sheet size; 'happy' changes 3.7 % of the face (a dark mouth on a dark muzzle).
The cloud reviewer (11-18) finds the toothed mane a little 'saw-back'; it can be softened into more of a brush if you agree.

Feet: fixed in the rig. The motion clip here predates the fix until the laptop re-renders the stress takes.
